A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EEG-FM-Bench. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching despite revisions and page shifts.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments in Section 4 and Tables 2–9, plus gradient, representation and qualitative analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports revised benchmark results, additional classifier-head results and retained original diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark retains its model adapters, fine-tuning strategies, task setups, classifier heads and diagnostic algorithms. Newly documented normalization conventions do not establish a method change; the revised numerical diagnostic settings concern evaluation protocol.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14 datasets across 10 paradigms, with matching dataset descriptions and Table 1. Additional SEED-VII classifier-head results extend an existing experiment within already represented task coverage.

E2.justification: Both evaluate BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, EEGPT, CBraMod, CSBrain and REVE, alongside Mantis and Moment. Tables 7–8 retain the same four head-ablation comparators: LaBraM, CBraMod, CSBrain and REVE.

E3.justification: v3 excludes LaBraM–SEED and EEGPT–SEED/PhysioMI pairs from Figure 1's aggregate performance. The reported CountSketch dimension changes from 6 to 1024, and the warm-up learning-rate factor changes from 0.1 to 0.5. These are limited protocol revisions; splits, metrics and the 30-epoch budget remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 7–8 add SEED-VII to the attention-pooling and large-MLP classifier-head ablations, extending evidence about decoder capacity. Existing adaptation and pretraining ablations receive revised outcomes, while the gradient, representation and qualitative case-study analyses retain their scope.

E5.justification: Both versions report performance means and standard deviations across five independent runs and diagnostic statistics across ten random seeds. No new uncertainty-estimation practice, confidence interval or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerous entries in Tables 2–8 change, and Section 4.6 switches the overall leader from EEGPT to REVE. For example, Table 3 replaces REVE's PhysioMI balanced accuracy of 30.63±0.06 with 58.82±0.45, and EEGPT's BCIC-2a value of 50.52±0.93 with 39.23±1.48. Tables 7–8 also add SEED-VII results. These are revised reported outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains, given the changed settings and aggregation.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(12) and the definitions of gradient alignment, conflict, subspace affinity, CKA, RSA and classification metrics are retained. Specifying projection dimension and PCA rank changes experimental documentation rather than mathematical theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace the claim that compact architectures consistently outperform larger models and challenge typical scaling laws with a protocol-qualified account: REVE leads on average, compact models remain competitive, and scale alone does not explain transfer. The central multi-task claims also explicitly acknowledge negative transfer.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 replaces the interpretation that architectural bias outweighs scale with an account allowing scaling benefits while acknowledging objective, architecture and adaptation confounds. v3 adds substantive discussion of pretraining overlap, protocol-dependent rankings and limited public EEG data for further scaling. Section 6 also identifies model-specific adaptation constraints, while retaining limitations already discussed in Appendix F.

D1.justification: Appendix B.6 newly documents model-specific amplitude normalization, including BENDR's min-max scaling and REVE's window-level z-score approximation. The reported hardware changes from two A800 GPUs to one; PCA rank 6 and Figure 1's data-volume estimation basis are also specified. These disclosures improve reproducibility without establishing that the newly described normalization procedures changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Markiewicz et al. (2021) on OpenNeuro to support discussion of the available pretraining-data supply. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works, including REVE, CBraMod and CSBrain; the related-work coverage is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory findings, substantial experimental discussion and conclusion are rewritten to present more conditional interpretations. v3 adds main-text Section 6 and Appendix C.1, while retaining Appendix F. Correspondence, publication headers and bibliographic wording are also updated; the benchmark pipeline and most appendix prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The figure and table inventory and overall visual design remain intact. Figure 1 and several radar charts are rescaled or redrawn, Figure 5 moves, Figure 10 gains a SEED-VII spoke, and Tables 2–8 gain overlap markers. Tables 7–8 add corresponding rows, while diagnostic and case-study figures remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important weaknesses in the benchmark's central comparisons by flagging pretraining overlap and excluding affected pairs from Figure 1. It replaces v2's categorical scaling conclusion with protocol-qualified interpretations consistent with the revised tables and documents checkpoint-specific normalization. Together, these changes substantially improve comparison transparency, reproducibility and the defensibility of the main conclusions; higher reported scores alone are not the basis for this assessment.
